title: Frontend: List Format
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind List Format. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(items) for strings. Empty gives empty text, one item itself, two use A and B, three or more use comma-separated prefix followed by , and LAST. This is a narrow English formatting contract.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
For a locale-aware product, use Intl.ListFormat with the intended style and type.
alternativeApproaches: Offer a count-limited summary that reports remaining items without confusing formatting with truncation policy.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty; one; two.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
